topic: Causal nullity and attainable-rank design in finite proximal treatment multigraphs. For binary outcomes, finite observed proxies, bounded finite latent support, eta-positive observed cells, and strictly positive full-data completions with common W-given-U kernels and shared treatment-node contrast bridges, prove target-population root contrasts are identified exactly when ker(A_P) is contained in ker(R_0). For every violating null direction, construct an explicit nonzero interval of positive full-data perturbations preserving all observed trial and target laws, proxy restrictions, and latent node contrasts while changing the target. In the rank-one trial submodel with common proxy kernel C of rank q, prove generic rank q(|V|-1) exactly when the treatment multigraph contains q edge-disjoint spanning trees; full W-bridge recovery also requires q=|W|. Give matroid-union certificates, separated-rank GLS/Wald inference, and finite-sample Bonferroni Clopper–Pearson cell-region projection covering every compatible contrast without rank selection. Consumer: the NETMOTION neonatal-oxygen IPD network, where added trials cannot overcome the proxy-rank ceiling. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Signed-cell causal lifts were derived and stress-tested on eight heterogeneous two-stratum/four-treatment rational models, preserving 5,120 observed cells and 2,304 latent-CATE equalities. Nonempty attainable-row sets have affine dimension q−1; 258 rectangular-kernel graph cases matched the q-tree rank formula. Rank-two/rank-three parallel-edge designs and exact binomial-tail inversion were checked, including 3,528 multinomial configurations. Boundaries involving q=1, redundant C rows, insufficient trees, zero Z-kernel entries, dependent outcomes, deficient rank, and denominator clearing were tested; no exact literature collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently prove the universal signed-cell lifting lemma for arbitrary finite supports, preserving every observed cell and shared latent node contrast simultaneously. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the supplied two-X/four-treatment rational model with dependent outcomes, a zero in a nonconstant Z kernel, and a nonreference left endpoint; apply both perturbation signs at half the explicit radius and verify every equality and positivity condition exactly. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_proximal_trialnetwork_nullity.md.

open_problems.open_problem: In a finite multigraph of randomized treatment comparisons with common finite proxy kernels and shared node-contrast bridges, characterize exactly which target-population root contrasts remain identified when bridge solutions are nonunique, and prove necessity by a strictly positive observed-law-preserving full-data perturbation for every violating null direction.

source_refs.claim: A proximal causal functional can be uniquely identified and root-n estimable even when the bridge integral equations admit multiple solutions.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Proximal indirect comparison identifies a target-trial treatment effect with shifted unobserved effect modifiers, but studies one source RCT and one target RCT rather than an arbitrary treatment multigraph.
source_refs.author: Zehao Su, Helene C. W. Rytgaard, Henrik Ravn, Frank Eriksson

source_refs.claim: Causally interpretable meta-analysis transports effects from multiple independent trials using observed effect modifiers but does not establish a proxy-bridge nullspace frontier.
source_refs.author: Issa J. Dahabreh, Sarah E. Robertson, Lucia C. Petito, Miguel A. Hernán, Jon A. Steingrimsson

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zhang et al. isolate strong identification of a linear causal functional despite a nonunique bridge, but do not treat multiple randomized treatment edges, target-population transport, or shared latent-node contrasts. Su et al. enter proximal trial transport only for a two-RCT indirect comparison, while Dahabreh et al. handle many trials using observed transport covariates. The missing proof step is a universal finite-support lifting argument showing that every algebraic null direction not annihilated by the target functional is realized by two strictly positive full-data laws preserving every trial and target cell, proxy restriction, and shared node contrast; operator nullity alone does not supply that causal completion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient identification theorem ker(A_P) ⊆ ker(R_0), an observed-data formula for every contrast satisfying containment, and an explicit two-sided positive perturbation interval for every violating direction.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from indirect comparison to failed transport through unobserved shifted effect modifiers and then to proxy bridges; the multigraph opportunity should retain that destination-first framing.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A target trial omits a treatment of interest -> ordinary conditional transportability can fail through unobserved effect modifiers -> proxies restore selected cross-trial contrasts -> determine exactly which contrasts survive in an arbitrary trial network

method_exemplars.technique: Represent bridge solutions as an affine solution set and prove that a linear causal functional is invariant over that set without bridge uniqueness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A target root contrast is likewise a linear functional of a nonunique finite bridge, making identification an annihilator-of-kernel question.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate primary and Riesz nuisances by penalized minimax methods and prove asymptotic normality for a strongly identified functional despite a weakly identified or nonunique nuisance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once a target contrast annihilates the multigraph bridge nullspace, it is a strongly identified linear functional of a weakly identified bridge.

open_problems.open_problem: For a rank-q common proxy kernel in a finite proximal treatment multigraph, characterize the least-cost additional randomized comparison edges needed to attain all q(|V|-1) identifiable node-contrast directions, and determine separately when the full W-indexed bridge is recoverable.

source_refs.claim: Finite-proxy proximal identification is governed by a proxy-matrix rank condition, making proxy rank an intrinsic information ceiling.
source_refs.author: Wang Miao, Zhi Geng, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: A graph packs q edge-disjoint spanning trees exactly under partition cut inequalities, providing a certificate for q-fold graphical connectivity.
source_refs.author: C. St. J. A. Nash-Williams
source_refs.venue: Journal of the London Mathematical Society

source_refs.claim: Graph Laplacians encode information for systems of pairwise treatment contrasts and support optimal design, but without proxy-rank multiplexing or proximal bridges.
source_refs.author: Samuel Rosa

source_refs.claim: NETMOTION synthesized 12 trials and 1055 infants over low, intermediate, and high initial-oxygen nodes, with low or very-low certainty for important mortality contrasts.
source_refs.author: James X. Sotiropoulos et al.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The proxy literature supplies rank conditions but does not connect attainable proximal contrast rank to treatment-network design. Classical tree packing certifies q-fold graph connectivity, and Rosa relates graph spectra to ordinary contrast information, yet the scan found no treatment-network result for a constrained incidence-proxy operator whose edge rows must lie in the attainable row space of a common proxy kernel. The first proof step that changes is converting the Nash-Williams partition certificate into the generic rank of that operator and proving constructively that attainable proxy rows realize each matroid-union basis. Full W-bridge recovery is a distinct objective and may remain impossible when q is below the number of W categories, regardless of added trial edges.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A generic-rank theorem giving rank q(|V|-1) exactly when the multigraph contains q edge-disjoint spanning trees, a matroid-union min-cost augmentation certificate, and a separate if-and-only-if condition q=|W| for full W-bridge recovery.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes the clinically consequential IPD treatment network concrete and foregrounds remaining uncertainty that motivates principled additions to the evidence network.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Small neonatal trials compare different initial-oxygen levels -> IPD network synthesis creates indirect comparisons but important contrasts remain uncertain -> proxies may address shifted latent modifiers yet impose an information ceiling -> choose new trial edges that attain every contrast the proxy rank permits

method_exemplars.technique: Use partition cut inequalities to certify q edge-disjoint spanning trees and interpret the packing as q independent graphic-matroid bases.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Full attainable rank consists of q independent copies of the |V|-1-dimensional treatment-incidence space.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate treatment-contrast information into weighted graph-Laplacian eigenstructure and optimize design criteria on that graph.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After the rank threshold is met, the graph-information correspondence can rank feasible edge augmentations by precision rather than rank alone.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce finite-proxy identification to matrix rank while allowing the measurement mechanism itself to remain unidentified.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The q-dimensional attainable proxy row space is the second matroidal factor in the incidence-proxy rank calculation.

open_problems.open_problem: When a target root contrast fails the finite proximal multigraph nullspace criterion, derive its sharp identified interval or polytope under bounded latent support, eta-positive observed cells, common proxy kernels, and shared latent node contrasts, including which boundary values are attained by strictly positive completions.

source_refs.claim: Proxy variables can bound causal effects without completeness or point identification of a bridge, but the construction is not a multi-trial treatment-network bound with shared node restrictions.
source_refs.author: AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: With two finite proxies a rank condition identifies the causal effect; failure of the condition motivates weaker conclusions rather than full bridge recovery.
source_refs.author: Wang Miao, Zhi Geng, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: The proximal bridge solution set may be non-singleton even when a mean functional is identified, making functional variation over that set central.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ghassami et al. replace completeness with proxy-based partial identification for a single-treatment setting, while Zhang et al. study invariance over nonunique bridge solutions. Neither incorporates a treatment multigraph, common W-given-U kernels across trials, shared latent node contrasts, or strict positivity of every full-data completion. Optimizing only over algebraic bridge solutions can be nonsharp because some solutions may lack latent completions; sharpness therefore requires a simultaneous causal lifting theorem and a proof that extrema, or their open-boundary limits under strict positivity, are realized.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-dimensional linear or polynomial-program representation of the sharp target-contrast identified set, with a theorem equating projected extrema to feasible positive full-data completions and reducing the set to a singleton exactly under the nullspace criterion.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames failure of completeness as an information frontier rather than a reason to abandon proxy analysis, which is the right arc from point identification to sharp network bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxy point identification relies on completeness -> completeness can fail and is not empirically testable -> proxies may still restrict the causal effect -> compute the sharp restriction for a transported treatment-network contrast

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize causal functionals over proxy-compatible latent laws without first identifying a bridge and prove validity and sharpness of the bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is the projection of a finite proxy-compatible completion set onto a target root contrast.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate projection inference for a scalar functional of a partially identified parameter and prove uniform asymptotic coverage while solving feasibility programs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proximal-network interval is a scalar projection of a constrained high-dimensional completion set.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop inference for target-root contrasts in finite proximal trial networks that is efficient under a separated nonzero-rank stratum but remains uniformly valid as nonzero singular values approach zero or the contrast becomes set identified, without preliminary rank selection.

source_refs.claim: A continuous linear functional can have root-n asymptotically normal inference even when its nuisance function is weakly identified or nonunique, under a strong-functional condition.
source_refs.author: Andrew Bennett, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Whitney Newey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, Masatoshi Uehara

source_refs.claim: Conditional-Wald critical values support inference under arbitrarily weak identification and heteroskedastic or clustered errors, with extensions to nonlinear GMM.
source_refs.author: David S. Lee, Justin McCrary, Marcelo J. Moreira, Jack Porter, Luther Yap

source_refs.claim: A debiased proximal estimator is regular and locally efficient without bridge uniqueness under additional regularity conditions, but the analysis does not cover network-rank transitions.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bennett et al. and Zhang et al. justify regular inference when a causal functional remains strongly identified despite a weak or nonunique bridge, whereas Lee et al. protect tests against weak identification in IV/GMM. None supplies one procedure for a finite proximal treatment multigraph whose estimability matrix can change rank and whose target switches from point to set identification at the boundary. A separated-rank pseudoinverse CLT is discontinuous at that boundary, while directly importing weak-IV critical values ignores positivity-constrained latent completions and the fact that selected linear functionals may remain identified.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A rank-stratified GLS or debiased estimator with an efficiency bound and Wald limit under singular-value separation, paired with an identification-robust inverted test or projection confidence set having uniform coverage over local-to-rank-deficient sequences and the exactly deficient model.

writing_exemplar.why: Its distinction between a weakly identified nuisance and a strongly identified functional cleanly frames why bridge-rank failure need not invalidate every target contrast.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conditional moments can weakly identify or fail to identify a nuisance bridge -> selected linear causal functionals may remain stable -> debiasing yields regular inference under strong-functional conditions -> make inference honest as a trial-network contrast crosses that stability boundary

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate primal and debiasing functions by penalized minimax criteria and prove root-n asymptotic linearity for the target functional rather than the nuisance bridge.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A nullspace-invariant root contrast can stay strongly identified while the bridge vector is not.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on identification-strength statistics and use data-dependent Wald critical values to control size under arbitrarily weak first-stage information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The smallest nonzero singular values of the proximal network operator play the role of first-stage strength and can drift to zero.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert calibrated feasibility tests and project directly onto a scalar functional with uniform asymptotic coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At exact rank deficiency the root contrast becomes an identified-set projection, requiring a transition from Wald to projection geometry.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a finite-sample confidence region for every target-root contrast compatible with a finite proximal treatment network by projecting simultaneous exact multinomial-cell regions through positivity, shared-kernel, and shared-node-contrast constraints, and quantify when the projection remains nonvacuous under deficient rank.

source_refs.claim: Exact binomial-tail inversion gives conservative finite-sample confidence limits for a cell probability.
source_refs.author: C. J. Clopper, E. S. Pearson

source_refs.claim: Calibrated projection gives uniformly asymptotically valid confidence intervals for scalar projections of partially identified parameters, but not exact finite-sample multinomial coverage.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: NETMOTION contains 1055 infants across 12 trials and reports low or very-low certainty for important oxygen comparisons, making sparse-cell coverage practically relevant.
source_refs.author: James X. Sotiropoulos et al.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Clopper-Pearson inversion is exact for one binomial margin, while calibrated projection methods are asymptotic and generally assume moment-model regularity. The scan found no exact procedure that simultaneously covers observed cells from heterogeneous trials and a target sample, intersects those cell regions with nonlinear latent-completion and common-kernel restrictions, and projects onto all compatible proximal contrasts without estimating rank. The unresolved proof step is showing that simultaneous marginal cell coverage propagates through a possibly disconnected, nonconvex feasibility correspondence even at zero counts, deficient rank, and nonunique bridges.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A Bonferroni-adjusted exact cell-region construction and projection algorithm with a finite-sample theorem covering every compatible target contrast at level at least 1-alpha for every rank, plus sufficient conditions for nonemptiness and shrinking diameter.

writing_exemplar.why: Its small, heterogeneous neonatal IPD network and low-certainty conclusions make finite-sample honesty and coverage of all compatible contrasts concrete.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A clinically important IPD network is assembled from small heterogeneous trials -> indirect oxygen contrasts remain low-certainty -> proxy adjustment adds rank and latent-feasibility uncertainty -> report an exact region covering every causally compatible contrast without selecting rank

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact binomial tails for each multinomial cell margin and combine the marginal events by Bonferroni to obtain a simultaneous finite-sample cell region.
method_exemplars.why_closest: All downstream causal constraints are deterministic once the trial and target cell-probability vector is fixed, so exact simultaneous coverage is preserved under set projection.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute scalar confidence limits by optimizing the target directly over a relaxed feasible parameter region instead of covering every nuisance coordinate tightly.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired output is a projection of a high-dimensional proximal completion region onto each root contrast.

literature_map:
Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018, Biometrika; arXiv:1609.08816) make finite-proxy rank central to proximal point identification and discuss weaker conclusions when rank fails.
Tchetgen Tchetgen et al. (2020, arXiv:2009.10982) formulate proximal g-computation through outcome bridges and completeness for point and longitudinal treatments.
Cui et al. (2024, JASA; arXiv:2011.08411) derive proximal efficiency bounds and doubly robust, locally efficient estimators under bridge conditions.
Kallus, Mao, and Uehara (2021, arXiv:2103.14029) and Ghassami et al. (2022, AISTATS; arXiv:2104.02929) use minimax learning to weaken parametric and uniqueness demands in bridge estimation.
Zhang et al. (2023, Statistics & Probability Letters; arXiv:2303.10134) prove that a causal mean may be identified and root-n estimable even when bridge solutions are nonunique.
Bennett et al. (2023, arXiv:2208.08291) extend this tension to strongly identified linear functionals of weakly identified conditional-moment nuisances.
Ghassami, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023, arXiv:2304.04374) derive proxy-based partial-identification bounds without completeness, but not for shared-bridge trial multigraphs.
Su et al. (2026, Biometrika; arXiv:2405.10773) establish proximal indirect comparison for one source and one target RCT with shifted unobserved effect modifiers.
Dahabreh et al. (2020, Epidemiology, and 2023, Biometrics; arXiv:1903.11455 and 1908.09230) transport effects from collections of trials using observed covariates, leaving the multi-trial unobserved-proxy intersection open.
Bareinboim and Pearl (2016, PNAS) give complete graphical data-fusion logic but not finite bridge-nullspace or positive-completion certificates.
Rosa (2018, AStA; arXiv:1612.06571) connects pairwise-treatment information to graph Laplacians and optimal design without a proxy-rank layer.
Nash-Williams (1961, JLMS) supplies the partition certificate for edge-disjoint spanning trees; matroid-union algorithms make packing constructive, but no located causal paper tensors it with attainable proxy rows.
Lee et al. (2023, arXiv:2311.15952) provide conditional-Wald inference under weak IV/GMM identification; Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica; arXiv:1601.00934) provide calibrated projection for partially identified functionals.
Sotiropoulos et al. (2024, JAMA Pediatrics; doi:10.1001/jamapediatrics.2024.1848) analyze NETMOTION's 12 trials and 1055 infants, with low or very-low certainty for important oxygen contrasts.
